record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are present; the linked documentation and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports the effect of a custom Arditi/Labonne-style weight orthogonalization on refusal behavior, but this is not the original single-direction activation projection.
record.gate_note: The README says the 465-prompt benchmark did not reach 0/465 and that refusals remain on hard prompts. The benchmark script is listed, but no benchmark results table or exact achieved count is given. The repository description claims 0/465 refusals, which conflicts with the README's account; per repo rules, that description is not recorded as a result row.
record.test_reason: It applies an Arditi/Labonne-style weight orthogonalization to a domain fine-tune of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a hybrid-attention MoE. It reports the effect on refusals only qualitatively: softened, not eliminated. This bears on V2 in a new architecture.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say simple Arditi/Labonne orthogonalization over 5 directions softened Qwen3.6's refusals but did not eliminate them, calling the model 'robustly aligned'. They make the Llama-Guard-3-1B gateway plus policy.yaml the primary enforcement boundary.
record.recipe_differences: A custom Arditi/Labonne-style weight orthogonalization rather than the original activation projection; it uses five directions and edits selected tensors across attention and MoE components.
record.problems: The refusal outcome is qualitative and lacks an achieved count or pre-edit baseline. No controls, uncertainty, or capability results for the abliterated model are reported. The repository description's 0/465 claim conflicts with the README's explicit account that this target was not reached.
record.rows_left_out: No results were reported for the listed refusal benchmark script beyond the qualitative statement recorded in r1; scripts and other evaluation files were not treated as results.

untested.parts: Exact refusal rate before and after the edit. Capability preservation of the abliterated model: no lm-eval results reported, and the calibration perplexity has no pre-edit comparison. Effect on the unmodified released base or instruct model.
Not tested as named: no single-direction activation ablation, no direction addition, no capability comparison.

missing.what: Quantitative refusal-benchmark outcome (465 prompts) before and after abliteration, and the postmortem details. Referenced but not in the text read.

record.verdict_notes: The repo description's 'Heretic-abliterated to 0/465 refusals' contradicts the README. The README says Heretic was incompatible and the 0/465 target was not reached; the README account is used here. The BF16 perplexity of 6.6283 on calibration data is reported without a pre-edit comparison, so it is not a capability-preservation result. Hackathon repo, not peer reviewed, no controls or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports refusal behavior after a five-direction weight edit, not the claimed single difference-in-means direction projected out at every layer and position. It does not test adding the direction or report whether other abilities are largely preserved.
No exact achieved refusal count or baseline refusal count is reported.

statements.correction: Subject: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Domain-Aggressive, a domain LoRA fine-tune of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (256 experts, top-8, 10 full-attention + 30 linear-attention layers). Each pass edits 121 tensors: embed_tokens, 10 self_attn.o_proj, 30 linear_attn.out_proj, 40 shared_expert.down_proj, 40 fused experts.down_proj (about 10,321 matrices). 5 directions from layers 36 to 32 give 605 tensor updates. Result: refusals softened but not eliminated, 0/465 not reached, no count given. The author's explanation is that the model is 'robustly aligned' and the pass was too weak, not missed weights.
statements.problem: The sentence about this study is right, but it is filed under 'removal depends on which weight matrices the edit reaches'. This edit already reached every residual writer, including all expert down_proj slices, and refusal still remained. So the study shows removal is incomplete even with full coverage, not that coverage decides it. The model is also a domain LoRA fine-tune, not the base Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.
